items.title: A coding relay a human can trust
items.description: Make the local Gemini-to-Claude-to-Codex workflow obvious, testable, and useful on a real repository.
acceptance_criteria: An operator can tell who is coding and why.
Only token or quota exhaustion advances the coding line.
A complete run remains reviewable after restart.

items.title: See the coding handoff
items.description: Put the active coder, standby order, and failover reason where an operator cannot miss them.
acceptance_criteria: The control room shows Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 5, and Codex in order.
The current worker and standby workers have different visual states.
The route remains understandable on a narrow screen.

items.title: Show the live coding line
items.description: Expose the selected coder and fallback order in the control room and run detail.
acceptance_criteria: Gemini 3.1 Pro is shown as the first coding worker.
Claude Sonnet 5 and Codex are shown in fallback order.
The display is derived from runtime configuration rather than a second routing rule.

items.title: Explain why a handoff happened
items.description: Record a short operator-facing reason when the coding worker changes or stops.
acceptance_criteria: Quota exhaustion is distinct from timeout, authentication, policy, and coding failures.
Ordinary failures stop and explain instead of selecting another coder.
The reason survives restart in durable evidence.

items.title: Prove the relay without spending tokens
items.description: Exercise every selection and recovery branch with deterministic providers before using paid accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Every handoff branch has an automated test.
Non-quota failures have tests proving that failover does not occur.
Interrupted runs recover with the same route and authority.

items.title: Test both quota handoffs
items.description: Simulate exhausted Gemini and Claude quotas and verify the exact next worker.
acceptance_criteria: Gemini quota exhaustion selects Claude Sonnet 5.
Claude quota exhaustion selects Codex.
The test records the route decision and does not invoke a live provider.

items.title: Test the stop paths
items.description: Prove that authentication, timeout, policy, and implementation failures do not silently consume the next provider.
acceptance_criteria: Each ordinary failure stops on the current worker.
The operator receives a useful reason and next action.
No additional coding task or worker is created.

items.title: Complete one field mission
items.description: Use the proven local workflow on one small repository and keep the evidence readable.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout can complete the mission using documented commands.
The final report ties the requested outcome to the diff and checks.
A human makes the final acceptance decision.

items.title: Run a small repository end to end
items.description: Choose one bounded task, let Gemini implement it, and inspect the complete local trail.
acceptance_criteria: The task has measurable acceptance criteria before execution.
Implementation occurs only inside the leased worktree.
Diff, checks, reviews, budget, and human decision appear in one report.

items.title: Fix the guide from field notes
items.description: Turn every confusing step found during the field mission into a short, tested instruction or a product fix.
acceptance_criteria: A second operator can repeat the mission from a clean checkout.
Every command includes the expected result.
Destructive recovery steps carry an explicit warning.
